cases.title: Fuse UTF-8 name-table traversal and QBE rendering
cases.scope: All 185 compiler and 150 Map constructor names, in exact captured order, rendered as the p111_cid_names_N string-data declarations. Old: current p111q_utf8 plus p111q_data. New: direct character-to-QBE byte text. Each n repeats both complete tables.
cases.whatWorkDisappears: Per-byte P111QByte objects, the UTF-8 reversed list/reversal, datum-to-String list construction and later fragment flattening. Decimal formatting and full final String remain.
cases.oracle: Exact canonical old/new String equality for every control; additional literal UTF-8 controls include empty, ASCII, 2/3/4-byte Unicode, embedded NUL/newline.
limitations: These are complete string-data definitions, not a whole backend or bounded native publication cursor.
Active P134 streaming also caps datum slices; this pure one-string screen does not establish peak-memory parity for long data rows.
The original table-building path materializes UTF-8 before later emission; moving construction changes lifetime and requires a future full native-request test.
n repetitions concatenate both distinct workloads; this output is a benchmark text corpus, not one linkable QBE program.

cases.title: Render repeated local spellings once per owner
cases.scope: Every N111Local occurrence in source traversal order in three complete authentic retained lexer scalar segments:12,10,13 operands. Cache is reconstructed separately for each owner and every n repetition.
cases.whatWorkDisappears: Repeated p111q_local special-name tests and %v_ String construction after the first identical spelling per owner.
cases.oracle: Exact canonical p111q_local output sequence, including every occurrence/newline. Independent fixed cache spelling oracle covers state, repeated name, empty name and Unicode.
limitations: This is a local-operand renderer kernel, not a whole-function emitter replacement; no non-local values are timed.
The three retained source inputs are native primitives/continuations from a Lexer compilation, not central Lexer control flow.
Linear cache search, exact String comparisons and fresh cache construction may cost more than formatting. These costs are included.
Numeric constants/labels are not cached in this bounded prototype; absent a local-name win there is no justification for broadening it.
